question: The acid and base which form sodium hydrogen carbonate are:
solution:
The correct answer is __**H2CO3 and NaOH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate, also known as baking soda, is formed from the reaction of carbonic acid (H2CO3) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH).
 
• Carbonic acid (H2CO3) is a weak acid formed when carbon dioxide (CO2) dissolves in water (H2O).
 
• Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is a strong base commonly used in various chemical reactions and industrial processes.
 
• The chemical reaction for the formation of sodium hydrogen carbonate is:

 H2CO3 + NaOH → NaHCO3 + H2O

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbonic Acid (H2CO3)**

 
 
• Carbonic acid is a weak acid that is formed when carbon dioxide (CO2) is dissolved in water (H2O).
 
• It plays a crucial role in the carbon cycle and is involved in the formation of caves and limestone structures.
 
• Carbonic acid is also present in carbonated beverages, giving them their fizz.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**
 
 
• Sodium hydroxide, also known as lye or caustic soda, is a strong base used in various industrial processes such as paper manufacturing, soap making, and water treatment.
 
• It is highly corrosive and can cause severe burns upon contact with skin or eyes.
 
• NaOH is commonly used in laboratories for titrations and pH adjustments.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate (NaHCO3)**
 
 
• Sodium hydrogen carbonate, commonly known as baking soda, is a white crystalline powder that is often used in baking as a leavening agent.
 
• It reacts with acids to produce carbon dioxide gas, which helps dough rise.
 
• NaHCO3 is also used in various household cleaning products and as an antacid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.
